newsitem.title: DENMARK: Copenhagen May bourse share trade up, bonds down.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen May bourse share trade up, bonds down.

text.p: Share trading on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange increased by 18 percent in market value year-on-year in May, while nominal bond turnover fell almost four percent, the bourse said on Wednesday.
It said in a statement that share trading in May was 20.6 billion crowns, seven percent up on April 1997 and 18 percent more than in May 1996.
Industrial, commerce and services and banking paper were the most actively traded, in that order, it added.
The bourse said that nominal bond turnover was 437 billion crowns in May, a fall of just under four percent compared with May last year, but an increase of two percent from April 1997.
"The strong dollar and the good performance of Danish companies and their solid earnings potential account for the increase in share trading," a Copenhagen Stock Exchange spokeswoman told Reuters.
She was unable to give an explanation for the decline in bond turnover in May. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
